Procedure: Attended, full-night diagnostic polysomnography.
Clinical Indication: Excessive daytime sleepiness, reported snoring, and witnessed apneas.

Impression: The findings are consistent with severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).

A follow-up appointment is recommended to discuss treatment options, including positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy. A subsequent PAP titration study under polysomnography is indicated to determine the optimal pressure for treatment.

Clinical History: 56-year-old female with a new 1.2 cm cluster of pleomorphic microcalcifications in
the left breast at the 10 o'clock position, identified on screening mammogram (BI-RADS 4C).
Diagnosis: Left Breast, 10 o'clock, Core Biopsy: Ductal Carcinoma in Situ (DCIS), intermediate nuclear
grade.
Gross Description: Received in formalin, labeled 'left breast cores,' are five tan-white, firm core
biopsies, ranging from 1.2 cm to 1.5 cm in length. A specimen radiograph confirms the presence of
microcalcifications corresponding to the area of concern. The cores are submitted entirely in one
cassette.
Microscopic Description: Sections show breast tissue with multiple ducts expanded and filled by a
monotonous population of atypical epithelial cells. The architecture is predominantly solid and
cribriform. The cells exhibit moderately enlarged, pleomorphic nuclei with irregular contours. Central
necrosis (comedonecrosis) is present within some of the involved ducts, associated with
psammomatous microcalcifications. No evidence of stromal invasion is identified in the tissue
provided.
Comment: The findings are diagnostic of Ductal Carcinoma in Situ. As this is a core biopsy diagnosis,
definitive grading and assessment of margins will be performed on the subsequent excision specimen.
Radiologic-pathologic correlation is recommended.

needle biopsy

Light Microscopy Description: The specimen consists of two cores of renal cortex and medulla. Up to 28 glomeruli are identified for evaluation. Immunofluorescence Description:
IgG: 3+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops (full house pattern).
IgA: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.

C1q: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.
Fibrinogen: Negative.
Albumin: Negative.
Electron Microscopy Description: Electron microscopy confirms diffuse subendothelial and mesangial electron-dense deposits. Tubuloreticular inclusions are present within endothelial cells. There is approximately 50% podocyte foot process effacement.
Comment: The combined findings are diagnostic of active, diffuse global lupus nephritis, ISN/RPS 2003 Class IV-G (A).

Clinical History: 28-year-old female with a one-month history of a painless, enlarging left-sided neck mass. Associated with night sweats. Concern for lymphoma.
Diagnosis: Lymph Node, Left Cervical, Excision: Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma, Nodular Sclerosis Type.
Gross Description: Received fresh, labeled 'left neck mass', is an encapsulated lymph node measuring 2.8 x 2.1 x 1.5 cm. The cut surface is tan-white and firm, with a vaguely nodular appearance.
Microscopic Description: Sections of the lymph node show complete effacement of the normal architecture by a nodular infiltrate. The nodules are defined by broad bands of collagenous fibrosis. Within the nodules, there is a mixed inflammatory background composed of small lymphocytes, eosinophils, and histiocytes. Scattered throughout this background are large, atypical cells, including classic binucleated Reed-Sternberg cells and their mononuclear variants (Hodgkin cells). These cells have large, vesicular nuclei, prominent eosinophilic nucleoli, and abundant cytoplasm.
Immunohistochemistry: The large, atypical cells show the following immunophenotype:
CD30: Positive
CD15: Positive
PAX5: Positive (dim)
CD45: Negative
CD20: Negative
CD3: Highlights the background T-cell population.
Comment: The morphologic findings in conjunction with the immunophenotype (CD30+, CD15+, PAX5+, CD45-) are diagnostic of Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma, Nodular Sclerosis subtype. Clinical correlation and appropriate oncologic management are recommended.
Specimen: Left cervical lymph node
